original_question: Can one prove special cases of one of the two conjectures discussed in Section 13 from known cases of the other conjecture?
target_in_paper: Section 13, Problem 13.2: "Prove one of the above two conjectures for some special case from the known case of the other conjecture."
correct_elements: Your draft correctly captures the core logical structure of Problem 13.2: the issue is to deduce a special case of one conjecture from an already known case of the other conjecture, and it is indeed about the pair of conjectures discussed immediately before Problem 13.2.
missing_details: The draft does not name the two conjectures: they are the Batyrev-Manin conjecture and the Malle conjecture.
It does not state the ambient scope: Section 13 is about the McKay correspondence over global fields, especially number fields.

It does not identify the objects counted by the two conjectures in the paper's nearby discussion: rational points of bounded height on a Fano-type variety over a number field, versus Galois extensions with bounded discriminant.
It does not specify the asymptotic parameter: the relevant bound tends to infinity (the height bound or discriminant bound, denoted abstractly by the bound in (13.1)).
It does not record the common asymptotic shape highlighted just before Problem 13.2, namely c B^a (log B)^{b-1}.
It does not make explicit that the desired implication may go in either direction: from a known special case of Batyrev-Manin to Malle, or from a known special case of Malle to Batyrev-Manin.
It does not indicate that this is meant in the paper's Section 13 framework, not as an arbitrary transfer principle between unrelated formulations of those conjectures.

No ambient ring, operator, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency conditions are relevant here; the missing stand-alone data are instead the arithmetic/geometric setting and the counting problems involved.
The phrase analogous to "for all sufficiently large m" does not occur here; the needed asymptotic quantifier is "as the relevant height/discriminant bound tends to infinity."
refined_question: In the global-field McKay-correspondence setting of Section 13, especially over number fields, can one prove, in a concrete special case, a case of the Batyrev-Manin conjecture for counting rational points of bounded height on a Fano-type variety from a known case of the Malle conjecture for counting Galois extensions with bounded discriminant, or conversely prove such a special case of the Malle conjecture from a known case of the Batyrev-Manin conjecture, where both counting functions are expected to have asymptotic form c B^a (log B)^{b-1} as the bound tends to infinity?
justification: The draft is aimed very specifically at Section 13, Problem 13.2, whose wording is essentially what your draft paraphrases. The immediately preceding discussion identifies the "above two conjectures" as the Batyrev-Manin conjecture and the Malle conjecture, in the context of the McKay correspondence over global fields, especially number fields. That same paragraph also explains what each conjecture counts and notes that both predict asymptotics of the form (13.1), i.e. c B^a (log B)^{b-1}, as the relevant bound goes to infinity. The introduction independently confirms that Section 13 is about relating the Batyrev-Manin and Malle conjectures through the global-field McKay-correspondence viewpoint. Since this paper does not itself state an equivalence reformulation of Problem 13.2, the safest paper-faithful rewrite is a sharpened stand-alone version of that problem rather than a new variant.
